# DC_STUB_KEEP -- the WIDE (town) keep list. GENERATED, do not edit.
#
#   python3 tools/dcstub/make_keeplist_town.py > tools/dcstub/keeplist-town.txt
#
# Rationale, and why a census cannot produce this list, is in the
# header of the generator. Short version: the town layout is drawn
# from the save's random seed, so a census names the acres ONE run
# happened to visit; and an unkept acre does not lose a texture, it
# loses its vertex array and renders nothing at all.
#
# This is a UNION with keeplist-opening.txt, which stays the list to
# use for size experiments and for title-screen work.
#
# Use:
#   DC_STUB_KEEP="$(grep -v '^#' tools/dcstub/keeplist-town.txt | paste -sd: -)"
#
# ⚠️ The mFM_grd_* ground textures are absent on purpose: R1 reads
# them off the disc (dc/src/dc_bgtex.c), both seasons, for no .bss.
# Adding them back costs 80,736 B and buys nothing.
#
# ⚠️ So are the VILLAGER npc/model/tex sets: R2 serves all 236 of
# them out of 16 slots (dc/src/dc_npctex.c). Re-adding one makes the
# pool skip that set, so the .bss returns for nothing. The SPECIAL
# NPC sets below (Tom Nook, the raccoons, end_1, kab_1, ...) are NOT
# pooled and MUST stay.
#
# ⚠️ And so are the VILLAGER npc/model/mdl species: R3 serves all 32
# out of 16 slots and relocates the 933 display-list words that name
# them (dc/src/dc_npcmdl.c). Same rule -- re-adding one makes the
# pool skip that species. The SPECIAL NPC models below are NOT
# pooled (their skeletons appear in no villager row) and MUST stay.
# ⚠️ R3, unlike R1 and R2, COSTS ~115,296 B of .bss: it restores
# geometry 31 species never had rather than freeing anything.

# ---- the rest of src/data/model, cheapest-first, up to the
#      900000 B budget (--full-model). These are the models the town
#      list never named: unkept they lose their VERTEX arrays and
#      collapse to the origin, which is the black spiky mess.
#      Affordable only because T1 (dc/src/dc_texpool.c) took
#      885,984 B of texture arrays out of .bss.
#      ⚠️ NOT EVERYTHING FITS. What the budget dropped still
#      renders as nothing; the kept/dropped byte counts go to
#      the generator's STDERR rather than into this file, so a
#      stale number cannot outlive the tree it was measured on.
